channel.title: PretzelerFL rides
channel.description: Curated ~25-minute habits/systems and presence/repair marriage ride briefings for PretzelerFL (Tobias / mowgli42, Melbourne FL). Best at 1.5× in Overcast — about 15–23 minutes of wall-clock listening. Home-life picks: habits, systems, focus, presence, repair. Not a workplace feed.
channel.author: Tobias / PretzelerFL / mowgli42

rides.title: Ride: Stay present when you shut down (Adam Young Part 2)
rides.summary: Christian counselor Adam Young names shutdown as going offline and social engagement—staying in contact—as the alternative. For dismissive-avoidant presence and repair.
rides.description: The Place We Find Ourselves ep 80 — Relational Conflict: Fight, Flight, Freeze, or Shut Down Part 2. Adam Young (Allender/Eldredge world) on shutdown vs staying in contact. From The Place We Find Ourselves.
rides.attribution: The Place We Find Ourselves — Adam Young

rides.title: Ride: Here but not really — fighting emotional absence
rides.summary: Matt & Sarah Hammitt on being physically home and emotionally gone—and choosing to stay and hear without defending. Presence after shutdown.
rides.description: FamilyLife Today: Here, but Not Really: Fighting Emotional Absence in Marriage – Matt & Sarah Hammitt. A Christian husband learns to stay present instead of checking out. From FamilyLife Today.

rides.title: Ride: Deep-Rooted Marriage — choose her again (WAH E825)
rides.summary: John Eldredge and Dan Allender on repair and choosing each other again after harm—including staying when the body wants to retreat.
rides.description: Wild at Heart E825 | The Deep-Rooted Marriage - Part 2. Eldredge + Allender on repair and presence when you want to leave the room. From Wild at Heart.

rides.title: Ride: Build atomic habits with James Clear
rides.summary: James Clear walks through habit formation, motivation, and why tiny consistent behaviors compound into identity-level change—core Atomic Habits ideas in a car-ride length.
rides.description: Atomic Habits author James Clear joins Chris Duffy to unpack the science of habit formation, how to work with your motivations, and why stacking small habits beats relying on willpower. From How to Be a Better Human (TED Audio Collective).
rides.attribution: How to Be a Better Human (TED Audio Collective) — 'How to develop the habits you want – and get rid of the ones you don’t (w/ James Clear)'

rides.title: Ride: Kick the procrastination habit
rides.summary: Motivation scientist Ayelet Fishbach shares research-backed cognitive tricks to stay engaged and finish what you start—practical anti-procrastination systems.
rides.description: Social psychologist Ayelet Fishbach explains the science of motivation and four proven tactics to interrupt the procrastination habit while staying happy and engaged. From TED Talks Daily.
rides.attribution: TED Talks Daily — '4 proven ways to kick your procrastination habit | Ayelet Fishbach'

rides.title: Ride: Three habits to escape your phone
rides.summary: Journalist Nayeema Raza offers three practical habits to restore curiosity and presence when phone use has become the default system running your day.
rides.description: Nayeema Raza describes how screens reshape attention and shares three habits to reignite curiosity, restore presence, and loosen phone addiction—followed by a short host interview. From TED Talks Daily.
rides.attribution: TED Talks Daily — '3 habits to practice curiosity — and escape your phone | Nayeema Raza'

rides.title: Ride: Power of Habit with Charles Duhigg
rides.summary: Pulitzer winner Charles Duhigg connects The Power of Habit loops to the productivity systems in Smarter Faster Better—cue, routine, reward applied to real work.
rides.description: Erik Fisher talks with Charles Duhigg (The Power of Habit; Smarter Faster Better) about habit loops and peak productivity practices for work and life. From Beyond the To-Do List.
rides.attribution: Beyond the To-Do List — 'Habits and Peak Productivity: Becoming Smarter, Faster, and Better with Charles Duhigg'

rides.title: Ride: Morning routines that actually work
rides.summary: Time-management expert Laura Vanderkam shares how high performers design morning routines that protect priorities before the day’s demands take over.
rides.description: Laura Vanderkam (What the Most Successful People Do Before Breakfast) discusses intentional morning routines and reclaiming time for what matters. From Beyond the To-Do List.
rides.attribution: Beyond the To-Do List — 'Morning Routines: What Successful People Do Before Breakfast with Laura Vanderkam'

rides.title: Ride: Cal Newport habit tune-up (phones, deep work, focus)
rides.summary: Cal Newport answers listener questions on de-addicting phones, keystone deep-work habits, making progress on big non-urgent projects, and training focus.
rides.description: A Deep Questions mini-episode habit tune-up: make an iPhone less distracting, install keystone habits for deep work, advance non-urgent big projects, and train focus. From Deep Questions with Cal Newport.
rides.attribution: Deep Questions with Cal Newport — 'Ep. 9: Habit Tune-Up: Dumbing Down Smartphones, Deep Habits, Progress on Non-Urgent Projects and Training Focus'

rides.title: Ride: Gretchen Rubin’s top habit-change tools
rides.summary: Gretchen Rubin and Elizabeth Craft survey the most effective habit tools—accountability, don’t-break-the-chain, tracking totals, and more—without one-size-fits-all advice.
rides.description: A special Happier episode on top tools for habit change: accountability partners, streak methods, tracking totals, and matching strategies to your tendency. From Happier with Gretchen Rubin.
rides.attribution: Happier with Gretchen Rubin — 'Happier - Ep. 410: Top Tools for Habit Change! New Year, Same You--Better Tools for Sticking to Our Good Habits'
